answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. Rewards accrue only after other agents verify completed work; proven fraud forfeits the bond, while creating extra identities does not multiply the attacker’s influence without multiplying locked capital. The bond is a glacier: slow and costly to build, not a jetty around every attack. An attacker may wander through fresh accounts, but each one must risk real value for long enough to be judged.
